sections.layout_rationale: New library lives in curriculum-standards-library/, parallel to the legacy flat curriculum_resources/. Florida, Arizona and IB use the same grade folder names and file names (grade-03/ela.json), so a Florida file, its Arizona twin, the IB file and the crosswalk are always at predictable sibling paths.

open_decisions.title: High school (Grades 9-12) is likely organized by course, not grade

options.label: Map courses to grades by typical sequence, flag as assumption
cons: Invents precision; courses are taken in varied order

options.label: Keep grade folders, organize each file by course, grade placement labeled C 'typical, not official'
cons: Some files hold several courses; grade files are uneven in size

options.label: Merge Grades 9-12 files by course
cons: Breaks the required grade folder structure and crosswalk symmetry

open_decisions.reasoning: It preserves your folder contract and the official course structure at once. The only cost is uneven file sizes. The template already has organization (by_grade | by_course) and grade_placement_label fields to support this.

open_decisions.title: IB PYP spans K-5, so six grades x four subjects give many near-duplicate files

options.label: Full separate files for every grade
pros: Simplest to consume; each file stands alone
cons: Heavy duplication; edits must be repeated six times; drift risk

options.label: Shared programme-level block referenced by each file, plus a short grade-specific Label C note
pros: Grade note makes clear the grade fit is ours
cons: Consumer must resolve the reference (the bundle can inline it)

options.label: Fewer files (one per programme and subject)

open_decisions.reasoning: PYP does not change year by year in the way state standards do. Sharing the official block avoids implying false grade-level differences. The IB template already has shared_programme_block_ref and grade_specific_note.

open_decisions.title: IB subject groups do not map one-to-one to our four subjects

options.label: Build the mapping table from official IB sources, mark every judgment Label C
cons: Needs access to IB framework documents; some may be restricted

options.label: Use one fixed mapping up front
cons: Would be written from memory, which the source rules forbid

open_decisions.reasoning: It is the only option consistent with your source rules. Expect MYP 'Individuals and societies' to relate to social studies and PYP transdisciplinary themes to span subjects, but confirm from ibo.org before recording.

open_decisions.title: Cloud sessions may restrict network access
open_decisions.finding: Tested 2026-10-02: fldoe.org, cdn.fldoe.org, cpalms.org, azed.gov and ibo.org are all blocked (proxy returned 403; WebFetch reports EGRESS_BLOCKED).

options.label: Environment network access set to Custom, add the five official domains (and keep package managers allowed)
pros: Least exposure; only official sources reachable
cons: A PDF may redirect to another host; may need one more domain later

options.label: Set network access to Full
cons: Broad access; also allows non-official sources, so rule discipline falls on us

options.label: Download PDFs yourself and add them to the repo
cons: Manual work from your phone; no live version checks

open_decisions.reasoning: Matches the 'official sources only' rule at the network level.

open_decisions.title: Reuse your existing Florida Grade 3-5 work (found while exploring the repo)
open_decisions.context: Branches primer-mvp and pre-mvp hold curriculum_resources/ with Florida Grade 3 ELA/math/science/SS, Grade 4 (ELA md+ts, math/science/SS ts) and Grade 5 ELA, as Markdown plus TypeScript seeds. It is not on this branch, so nothing here overwrites it.

options.label: Convert legacy files to the JSON envelope, then re-verify each standard ID and text against CPALMS
pros: Per-standard CPALMS URLs give fast checks
cons: Legacy files contain app-oriented extras (primer notes, misconceptions) that must be split into Label C or dropped

options.label: Ignore legacy and re-collect from scratch
Convert without re-verifying
cons: Violates the official-sources rule; unknown accuracy

open_decisions.reasoning: Keeps the work and satisfies the source rules. Legacy .ts SubjectSeed files keep feeding the app unchanged; the library becomes the verified source they are later generated from.
